captions.text: 1910: Wadai is still at war with the French.
1910: the seat moves to Simpsonhafen (Rabaul), infobox 1910-1914.
1910: Knud Rasmussen and Peter Freuchen set up a trading post at North Star Bay (Thule).
1910: Kasanje is absorbed into Portuguese Angola.
1910: Kasanje is incorporated.
1910: the monarchy falls and the Portuguese Republic takes over Portugal and its overseas territories.
1910: Russia occupies Urmia and Khoi.
1910: the Qing occupy Lhasa.
1910 (15 January): the federation of French Equatorial Africa is formed.
1910: Mozambique is a 'Territory of the Portuguese Empire (1505-1951)', the 'Province of Mozambique (1893-1926)', 'extending from Lourenço Marques in the south to Niassa in the north'.
February 1910: Qing troops enter Lhasa.
1910: the British give up the interior of British Somaliland to the Dervishes (mirror of dervish-state ledger 4, which dates it March-April 1910).

March-April 1910: the British evacuate the interior and the Dervishes hold it. Somaliland campaign page: "the British government ordered the evacuation of the internal regions of Somaliland" "between March and April 1910"; the Dervish state page: the British "retreated to the few remaining coastal regions", leaving "the interior regions in the hands of the Dervishes".
1910: the Union of South Africa is founded on 31 May.
1910: the Union of South Africa.
31 May 1910: the Union of South Africa leaves the British Africa umbrella (mirror of the south-africa dossier's found event, counterpart british-africa).
31 May 1910: the Cape Colony joins the Union of South Africa.
31 May 1910: the Colony of Natal becomes Natal Province of the Union of South Africa.
31 May 1910: the colony enters the Union of South Africa as the Orange Free State Province.
31 May 1910: the Transvaal Colony becomes the Transvaal Province of the Union of South Africa.
1910 (10 June): the Lado Enclave comes under the Sudan.
1910: the Lado Enclave passes to the Anglo-Egyptian Sudan.
1910: the Lado Enclave passes to the Sudan.
1910: the Korean protectorate ends in annexation, 29 August 1910.
1910: Japan annexes Korea.
1910: Korea is annexed by Japan.
1910: the Korean Empire ends.
28 August 1910: the principality becomes a kingdom.
1910: the republican uprising of 5 October overthrows King Manuel II and Portugal becomes a republic.
5 October 1910: the monarchy falls.

All of Angola without Cabinda and the Kongo country: the province as the treaties fixed it ('Agreements concluded with the Congo Free State, the German Empire and France in 1885-1886 fixed the limits of the province'; the south-east frontier by the Anglo-Portuguese treaty of 1891 and the 1905 arbitration award), without Cabinda, and without the Mbanza Kongo country, which the Kongo monarchy holds
the Republic's first Cliopatria shape (metropole, Azores, Madeira, Cabo Verde, Guinea, Sao Tome, Angola, Mozambique, Goa and Timor) taken back to the proclamation of 5 October 1910

1911: Yan Xishan takes Shanxi in the Xinhai Revolution.
1911: the Idrisi lose the two towns.
1911: Barotseland joins Northern Rhodesia.
1911: the capital is to move from Calcutta to Delhi.
1911: Bulozi proper joins Northern Rhodesia.
1911: Gowa loses its independence.
1911: the vassal sultanate becomes a Dutch East Indies regency (same sentence).
1911: the Geledi sultanate is incorporated into Italian Somaliland.

1911: the kingdom becomes a province of Northern Rhodesia.
1911: the Maderistas hold ground in Chihuahua.

1911: the Nri Kingdom ends as a political power.
1911: Gowa loses its independence.

1911, January: Liberia cedes the Parrot's Beak area to Sierra Leone.
11 February 1911: the protectorate ends when the Dutch abolish the sultanate ('Abolished by the Dutch: 11 February 1911'; 'The Dutch officially annexed the sultanate').
1911: the Dutch abolish the Riau-Lingga Sultanate.
April 1911: the Maderistas besiege Ciudad Juárez.
21 May 1911: the Treaty of Ciudad Juárez is signed, which ends the fighting at Ciudad Juárez.
May 1911: the Maderista revolt ends and the zone returns to the federal state.
21 May 1911: the Treaty of Ciudad Juárez ends the Maderista revolt.
1911 (4 October): Italian forces land on the shores of Libya, and 'With a decree of 5 November 1911, Italy declared its sovereignty over Libya.'
October 1911: Dud Murra surrenders.
1911 (October): Dud Murra surrenders.
1911: Italy declares war on the Ottoman Empire and lands in Libya.
1911 (4 October): the Italo-Turkish War reaches Libya.
3 October 1911: Italy bombards Tripoli.
October 1911: Dud Murra surrenders.
November 1911: France cedes a slice of the Middle Congo to Germany after the Agadir Crisis.
4 November 1911: the ceded Congo lands go to Kamerun.
4 November 1911: France receives the Fort Lamy strip in the same accord.
4 November 1911: Neukamerun.
4 November 1911: in the same accord Germany ceded 'a small area of territory to the southeast of Fort Lamy' to French Chad.
1911: Outer Mongolia declares independence from the Qing and the Bogd Khan is enthroned.
1911: the Tuvan nobles proclaim an Uryankhay republic.
1911: Outer Mongolia leaves the Qing.
Khalkha with Urga, the Provisional Government of Khalkha proclaiming the end of Qing rule on 1 December 1911; the Uliastai and Khovd garrisons still Qing
11.1 M km2, the last Cliopatria shape.
the shape With the full extent (the country plus the Alaska region), so that the Great Lakes waters inside Michigan and Wisconsin stay American.
1912: Tangier is set apart from the French and Spanish protectorates.
1912: the southern half of the Lado Enclave goes to Uganda.
1912: "The 1912 reform created a new governorate", Kholm (Chelm), from parts of the Sedlets and Lublin governorates, taken out of the Kingdom.
1912: Dar al Kuti ceases to be a protectorate.
1912: France annexes Dar al Kuti.

1912: Dar al Kuti is annexed.

1912: the Qing banner status ends with the dynasty.

1912: Tangier is excluded from the protectorates.
1911-1912: 'Italo-Turkish War; the empire loses its North African territories and the Dodecanese.'
1912: the Portuguese complete the occupation of the north-east.
1912: the Qing garrison at Lhasa surrenders.
1912: Tibet's tie to the Qing ends with the dynasty.
1912: United States Marines occupy Nicaragua.
1912: the occupation becomes annexation.

January 1912 (or late December 1911): the Qing governor of Uliastai leaves.
1912: the Kumul Khanate passes to the Republic.
1912: the khanate continues as a vassal of the Republic of China.

1912: the Kwantung lease outlives the dynasty (the end here is the Qing's, not the lease's).
1912: the lease of the New Territories outlives the dynasty and passes to the Republic (the end here is the Qing's, not the lease's).
1912: the lease of Guangzhouwan outlives the dynasty and passes to the Republic (the end here is the Qing's, not the lease's).

1912: the Qing abdicate and the Republic takes the empire's China.
1912: the Kumul khanate becomes the Republic's vassal.
30 March 1912: Morocco becomes a French protectorate.
30 March 1912: the Treaty of Fez makes Morocco a French protectorate.
1912: the government moves from Nanjing to Beijing.
August 1912: Khovd falls.
August 1912: Qing forces leave central Tibet.
1912: the Qing fall, and Chinese control of western Kham passes to the Republic.
1912: the Republic holds Chamdo and western Kham, west of the Yangtze.
1912: Chamdo and western Kham stay in Chinese hands under the Republic until 1918.
October 1912: the First Balkan War opens the Greek front in Epirus and Macedonia.
21 October 1912: Preveza is taken.
1912: the Treaty of Ouchy ends the war on 18 October.
18 October 1912: the Treaty of Ouchy ends the war.
1912 (18 October): the Treaty of Ouchy ends the war.
1912 (18 October): the Ottomans give up Libya.

8 October 1912: Greece joins the Balkan League's attack.
8 October 1912: Serbia joins the Balkan League's attack.
18 October 1912: the Treaty of Ouchy ends the war.
October 1912: the interior stays out of Italian hands.
18 October 1912: the Ottomans give up Libya.
October 1912: Ottoman Tripolitania ends.
1912: Bulgaria joins the First Balkan War and its armies enter Thrace and Macedonia.
October 1912: the Senussi hold the Cyrenaican interior as the Ottomans leave.
October 1912: the interior stays out of Italian hands.
1912: the Serbian army overruns Kosovo, Vardar Macedonia and the Sandžak.
28 November 1912: the Assembly of Vlorë declares Albania independent.
9 November 1912: Thessaloniki surrenders.

27 November 1912: the Spanish protectorate in northern Morocco is set up. It 'was established on 27 November 1912 by a treaty between France and Spain'; 'The surface area of the Protectorate was about 20,000 km2'; capital Tetuan.
27 November 1912: the Spanish protectorate in northern Morocco and the Cape Juby strip.
1912: the Serbian army takes the Albanian coast.
17 December 1912: Ouanda Djallé falls.
17 December 1912: the end per the page's body; the infobox gives 1830-1911 with "Final surrender of Kamun, Senussi's son".
the Sudan with Halaib; the southern half of the Lado Enclave ceded to Uganda in 1912, its northern half inside the South Sudan outline
the Kingdom without the Chelm Governorate (1912)
the 1912 shape without the Ioannina district and Samos, which fell in March 1913
Cliopatria's 1912 shape without the south-western Libyan block that no page shows under French rule
Eritrea, the Benadir coast and the Somali interior of the 1894 sphere (the 1900 correction) and, in Libya, only the five coastal enclaves; the 2,946 interior cells are removed
Tripolitania and Cyrenaica without the Sarra triangle
the 1912 shape without the Shkodër district, 'the newly captured city of Shkodër' that Montenegro had to abandon

90,944 km2: Serbia plus the lands its army held by the end of 1912 (Kosovo, Vardar Macedonia, the Sandžak and the northern Albanian coast, 25 cells of which it left in 1913).
275 km2 (one cell) against the infobox 382 km2 (undated; ratio 0.72, accepted: the zone is smaller than a grid cell can show).

1913: Imam Salim ibn Rashid al-Kharusi revives the Imamate of Oman at Nizwa and rebels against Muscat.
1913: the Ottomans renounce sovereignty over Qatar and Sheikh Abdullah bin Jassim Al Thani rules the peninsula.
1913: the interior passes from Muscat to the Imamate.
1913: the rebellion against the Sultan begins and runs to 1920.
1913 (Cliopatria's year): Cliopatria drops about 438 cells (Saudi Arabia 317, Qatar 48, Kuwait 37). The Partition page says Saudi Arabia 'annexed al-Ahsa and Qatif' without a date.
1913: about 117 Arctic cells (lon 80-105 E, lat 78-81 N) enter the shape.
1913: the interior secedes.
1913: the rebellion against Muscat begins and runs to 1920.
1913: the Emirate of Riyadh becomes the Emirate of Nejd and Hasa.
1913: Ibn Saud takes al-Hasa and Qatif from the Ottomans.
1913: the 13th Dalai Lama proclaims Tibet independent.
6 March 1913: Ioannina falls.
16 March 1913: Samos is Greek.
March 1913: the fighting on the Greek-Ottoman front ends with Ioannina (6 March) and Samos (16 March); the Treaty of London that ended the war is not dated on the pages opened for Greece.
May 1913: Montenegro gives up Shkodër.
30 May 1913: Montenegro and Serbia split the Sanjak of Novi Pazar.
May 1913: the war with the Ottomans ends for Montenegro with the loss of Shkodër and the split of the Sandzak (30 May 1913); the Treaty of London is not named on the page opened.
30 May 1913: the Treaty of London ends the war: 'all European territory of the Ottoman Empire west of the' Enos-Midiya line (Enez-Kıyıköy) is ceded to the Balkan League.
30 May 1913: the Treaty of London ends the war with Greece.
30 May 1913: the Treaty of London ends the war with Serbia; the League's division of the land was left open and led to the Second Balkan War (16 June 1913).

30 May 1913: 'Every Aegean island belonging to the Ottoman Empire, with the exception of Imbros and Tenedos,' goes to Greece, which also gains southern Epirus, southern Macedonia and Kavala (Treaty of Bucharest, 10 August 1913).

1913: 'Macedonia was divided among the Balkan states'; Serbia gained northeastern Macedonia and the eastern half of the Sanjak of Novi Pazar at Bucharest (10 August 1913) and Montenegro the western half.
1913: Bulgaria kept 'part of Macedonia (including Strumnitza) and western Thrace with its Aegean coastline, including Alexandroupolis' at Bucharest.
1913: the Treaty of London cedes the Ottoman lands to the Balkan League; Bulgaria keeps western Thrace and part of Macedonia.

1913: the First Balkan War ends on 30 May 1913 (Treaty of London); Serbia keeps Kosovo, Vardar Macedonia and the eastern half of the Sandžak, and the occupation of these lands becomes annexation (next event).
1913: Serbia annexes Kosovo, central Vardar Macedonia and 'the eastern half of the Sanjak of Novi-Pazar'.
June 1913: the Second Balkan War.
1913: Bulgaria attacks Serbia and Greece, opening the Second Balkan War.
1913: Bulgaria and Greece fight over Aegean Macedonia in the Second Balkan War.
1913: Bulgaria attacks Serbia and Greece on 16 June 1913 and the Second Balkan War begins ('attacked its former allies, Serbia and Greece, on 16 June 1913', First Balkan War page).
June 1913: Romania enters the Second Balkan War.
July 1913: the Great Powers recognise Albania within borders they draw, the Balkan League armies having occupied the land.
29 July 1913: the Anglo-Ottoman Convention defines Kuwait.
1913: Romania invades Bulgaria.

9 August 1913: Dul Madoba, the last clash with "the only remaining British mobile force in the colony" (Somaliland campaign page); the British had evacuated the interior in March-April 1910 and the Dervish state page has the walled town at Taleh built "in 1913, after the British withdrawal to the coast".
10 August 1913: the Treaty of Bucharest ends the Second Balkan War ('concluded on 10 August 1913').
10 August 1913: Greece gets eastern Macedonia.
10 August 1913: the Treaty of Bucharest confirms Metohija.
10 August 1913: the Treaty of Bucharest 'established the independent state of Albania' (Albania became independent under Great Power sponsorship).
1913: the Treaty of Bucharest ends the Second Balkan War.
1913: Bulgaria gives up Kavala and Eastern Macedonia to Greece.
1913: Bulgaria and Greece stop fighting at Bucharest.
1913: Romania takes Southern Dobruja.
1913: the Dobruja war with Romania ends at Bucharest on 10 August 1913.
1913: the Treaty of Bucharest is concluded on 10 August 1913; the frontier follows the Vardar-Struma watershed and 'the upper valley of the Strumica remained in the possession of Bulgaria'.
1913: Serbia keeps the Vardar Macedonia lands east of its 1912 line.
10 August 1913: the Treaty of Bucharest ends the war ('concluded on 10 August 1913').
10 August 1913: Romania gains Southern Dobruja.

30 September 1913: the Treaty of Constantinople returns Adrianople: 'Lozengrad, Lyule Burgas-Buni Hisar, and Adrianople reverted to the Ottomans' after the Ottomans won back Thrace in the Second Balkan War (the page gives no July date).
1913: Lozengrad, Lyule Burgas and Adrianople go back to the Ottomans.
1913: the Bulgarian-Ottoman contest over Thrace ends with the Treaty of Constantinople on 30 September 1913.
1913: Serbia leaves Albania under Great Power pressure.
14 December 1913: Crete is taken over.
113,618 km2 against the Treaty of Bucharest page's 108,610 km2 for Greece after the war (ratio 1.05).

6 August 1914: the Allies invade Kamerun.

1914: Austria-Hungary invades Serbia.
1914: South Africa invades South West Africa.
October 1914: Greek forces enter southern Albania.
November 1914: Britain lands at Fao and takes Basra.
November 1914: British forces hold ground in Khuzestan.
November 1914: the Fezzan is lost.

5 November 1914: the occupation of Cyprus ends in annexation (next event).
5 November 1914: Britain annexes Cyprus.

1914: the British occupation becomes a protectorate.

1914: the Serbs win the campaign.
19 December 1914: Egypt becomes a British protectorate.

1914: the invasion of East Prussia is defeated at Tannenberg.
1914, April: Tannu Uriankhai becomes a Russian protectorate.
April 1914: 'In April 1914 Tannu Uriankhai was formally accepted as a protectorate of Russia.'
2 August 1914: Germany occupies Luxembourg.
4 August 1914: Germany invades and occupies Belgium.
August-September 1914: the Pacific colonies fall.

1914: New Zealand occupies German Samoa.
September 1914: 'Australian troops occupied German New Guinea the following month' (after the invasion of Samoa in August).
1914: Australian forces seize German New Guinea.
1914: Australia occupies German New Guinea.
1914: Japan occupies German Micronesia: infobox 'Japanese occupation: 29 September 1914'; 'Japan occupied most of the remaining German possessions in the Pacific.'
1914, September: Russia wins the Battle of Galicia and begins the siege of Przemysl.
October 1914: 'Japanese troops occupied the German possessions in Micronesia in October 1914'.
October 1914: 'Japanese troops occupied the German possessions in Micronesia in October 1914' (the Marshall Islands among them).
November 1914: Jiaozhou Bay.

26 August 1914: French troops hold the east of Togoland.
26 August 1914: British troops hold the west of Togoland.

1915: South Africa captures German South West Africa.
1915: an Ottoman-Bulgarian agreement hands Bulgaria the Ottoman land west of the Maritsa.

May 1916: the United States occupies the Dominican Republic.

1916 (June): both districts are in Belgian hands.

10 June 1916: the Arab Revolt and the kingdom.

1916 (20 July): Britain and France divide German Kamerun.

1916: Mecca is taken.

28 August 1916: Romania invades Transylvania.

1916 (September): the Central Railway belt passes to the British occupation.
1916: Ta'if is taken.
1916: the Red Sea ports fall.
1916: Bulgaria seizes Dobruja from Romania.

1 September 1916: Mackensen's army 'attacked north from Bulgaria, starting on 1 September'; 'Bulgarian troops (aided by the German-Bulgarian Detachment) surrounded and stormed the fortress of Turtucaia' and 'The Romanian garrison surrendered on 6 September'; Constanta was 'occupied by the Central Powers on 22 October'.
25 October 1916: 'by 25 October the Romanian army was back to its initial positions' (Romanian Campaign page).
25 October 1916: the Romanian army is back at its start line.
3 November 1916: Qatar becomes a British protectorate.
5 November 1916: Germany and Austria-Hungary proclaim the Kingdom of Poland on the occupied land.
3 November 1916: Qatar becomes a British protectorate.
21 November 1916: 'the German cavalry entered Craiova'.
6 December 1916: Bucharest is captured.
27 December 1916: British Togoland is administered with the Gold Coast.
27 December 1916: Togoland is divided into British and French zones.
27 December 1916: the British zone is administered as part of the Gold Coast.
1916: the Russians retake the Hamadan front.

6 December 1916: 'Bucharest was captured on 6 December by Falkenhayn's cavalry'; by the end of the year 'Southern Romania, including Oltenia, Muntenia, Dobruja, and southern Moldavia, was now in the hands of the Central Powers'; 'The Germans were able to repair the oil fields around Ploiesti'.
December 1916: the government leaves for Iasi.
1916: a British force invades Darfur.
1916: Darfur is annexed.
1916: Ali Dinar is killed and Darfur's resistance ends ('the British conquered Darfur in 1916 and Dinar was killed in battle'; no month on the page).
1916: the British invade Darfur.

the whole Sudan with Darfur, Halaib and the Sarra triangle
The Congo alone; Ruanda-Urundi is Belgian-occupied enemy territory, drawn hatched from the occupation events, until the mandate of 20 July 1922
British Africa without Egypt and the occupied German colonies, the Union of South Africa and the Dervish-held interior of British Somaliland; without Libya except the Sarra Triangle

Unverified: page budget.

the colony of 12 January 1916: 'Ocean Island on 27 January 1916, along with the northern Line Islands', and 'During the year 1916, the Union Islands (Tokelau) were also annexed'; Christmas Island 'annexed it to the colony' on 28 November 1919
the towns the Sharifian army took in 1916: Mecca, Jeddah, Ta'if, Rabigh, Yanbu and al Qunfudhah, each a radius around the town (the page gives towns, not a frontier)
the kingdom of 1913-1915, occupied by Austria-Hungary from 15 January 1916 to October 1918
the shape plus Chukotka (the Chukchi Autonomous Okrug), which the 1778 gain (ledger/26) adds and Cliopatria's shapes only draw in part (about 410 cells of the okrug lie outside them)

1917: Ober Ost grows.
1917: the Tianjin concession is lost; the colonies page gives no loss date ('The source does not state a loss date or outcome').
1917: the United States gives up its territorial claims in the Thule area.
1917: the Treaty of Acroma.
1917: 'Russia withdraws from Anatolia under the Treaty of Brest-Litovsk' (main article); the Russian pages give 1918 for the return to the pre-war borders.
1917: Allenby's British forces defeated the Ottomans 'in 1917 in the Sinai and Palestine campaign' and occupied Palestine and Syria (the page gives no month for Jerusalem).
1917 (Cliopatria's year): the Partition page gives no date for Baghdad; at San Remo in 1920 'Britain also received Mesopotamia and Iraq.'
1917: the Russian occupation of Tabriz collapses.
1917: the Russian occupation of Urmia and Khoi ends with the collapse of the Russian army ('no effective military force' for the rest of 1917).
1917: the Russian zone across northern Persia dissolves; about 1,000 loyal Cossacks under Baratov still helped the British in February 1918.
1917: Sun Yat-sen sets up a rival government at Guangzhou.
1917: the Treaty of Acroma.
1917: British forces conquer southern Ottoman Syria.
1917: Wejh is taken.

8 January 1917: 'Mackensen's troops were able to capture Focsani on 8 January' (the year follows the page's Brăila entry of 5 January 1917), but 'an attempt to break the Siret River line on 19 January failed'; the Romanian line then held in Vrancea (Marasti 24 July 1917, Marasesti to 3 September 1917).
February 1917: the campaign ends.

March 1917 (dossier boundary): the Russian Empire falls (russian-empire dossier /ledger/137, dissolve to russian-republic) and its hold on the remainder of Galicia and Bukovina passes to the Provisional Government, recorded in the next two events.

March 1917 (bridge): the Russian-held remainder of Galicia and Bukovina continues under the Provisional Government, the state that launched the offensive of 29 June 1917 ('Russian Provisional Government'; Kerensky Offensive page).
11 March 1917: the British enter Baghdad.
March 1917: the Tsar falls.
March 1917: the same ground is now Russian Republic land under German occupation; Ober Ost was reorganised 'In March 1917 ...
1917, March: the empire falls.
31 March 1917: the Virgin Islands.
February-April 1917: the Germans fall back to the Hindenburg Line.
February-April 1917: the German armies withdraw to the Hindenburg Line.
June 1917: the Albanian protectorate.
1917: Aqaba falls.
14 August 1917: China, having declared war on Austria-Hungary and Germany, occupied the concession and declared the concessions 'revoked on 14 August 1917'; it was handed over at 16:00 that day.

3 August 1917: 'The Germans launched their counteroffensive against the Southwestern Front on 19 July', 'Austro-German troops took the city of Tarnopol on 25 July' and Czernowitz 'fell on 3 August'; 'Most of the Austro-Hungarian provinces of Galicia and Bukovina were retaken'; Kornilov stabilised the front 'by mid-August'.
1917: Sun Yat-sen sets up a rival military government at Guangzhou.
1917, 14 September (1 September O.S.): Kerensky proclaims the Russian Republic.
24 October 1917: the Austrians break through at Caporetto.
October-November 1917: Caporetto.

1917, 7 November: the Russian Soviet Republic is proclaimed in Petrograd after the October Revolution; the Soviet republic is proclaimed again on 25 January 1918 by the Third All-Russian Congress of Soviets.
1917: the Fourth Regional Muslim Congress at Kokand proclaims Turkestan an autonomous territory.
1917, 20 November (7 November O.S.): the Central Rada's Third Universal proclaims the Ukrainian People's Republic, still as autonomy 'within the Russian Republic'.
23 November 1917: the German force leaves German East Africa.
23 November 1917: Lettow-Vorbeck invades Portuguese Mozambique.
November 1917: the Germans leave the colony and the British hold the rest of German East Africa.
1917 (November): the south passes to the British occupation.
November 1917: Lettow-Vorbeck's German column enters Mozambique.
1917, 7 November: the Bolsheviks seize power and the republic's government is dissolved.
1917 (November): the south falls.
1917: the Alash Autonomy is proclaimed.
1917, 6 December: Finland declares independence.

1917, 24-25 December: the Soviet government of Ukraine is founded at Kharkiv, rival of the Kiev-based Ukrainian People's Republic: "The government of the Ukrainian Soviet Republic was founded on 24-25 December 1917."
1917, 6 December: "the Finnish Parliament approved the Declaration of Independence" after the collapse of the Russian monarchy; the Grand Duchy becomes the Republic of Finland.
The 1912 outline without the Tianjin concession; Romanian Wallachia is occupied (ledger), not annexed

Cliopatria shape of 1917 minus all of Canada except Newfoundland and Labrador, which stay a separate British colony; New Zealand; Kuwait; without the German New Guinea land that Cliopatria adds to the British shape from 1915; without the Indonesian cells of Cliopatria's shape

captions.text: 1918: Hungary leaves the Dual Monarchy as the Hungarian Democratic Republic.
1918: the Republic of German-Austria arises from the Dual Monarchy.
1918: the principality becomes the Free State of Schaumburg-Lippe in the German Revolution (the page gives the year, not the day).
1918: Zhang's control of Manchuria is complete.
Spring 1918: the German offensive retakes ground.
Spring 1918: the offensive in the west retakes ground.
1918: Tripolitanian rebels found a republic.
1918: the Belgian army occupies a zone of the Rhineland.
1918: Ma'an and its hinterland pass to the Hejazi claim.
1918: the Hejaz and the Saudis fight over al-Khurma.
1918: the Margraviate of Moravia ends (infobox 'Disestablished: 1918') and becomes Moravia Land in Czechoslovakia; its autonomy was eliminated in 1949.
1918: the Mutawakkilite Kingdom of Yemen 'became independent in 1918'; the Treaty of Sèvres acknowledged it.
1918: the Ottomans recover the north-east.
1918: British forces reach northern Persia.
1918: Lhasa takes back Chamdo and western Kham.
1918: the capital moves from Petrograd to Moscow (infobox: Petrograd 1917-1918, Moscow 1918-1991).
Late 1918: the Greater Poland uprising.
1918: Saudi and Ikhwan forces fight the Hashemites for al-Khurma.
1918: the Chinese occupation of western Kham ends and Lhasa holds the land again.
1918: Ukraine takes Polesia at Brest-Litovsk.
1918: the capital returns from Iasi to Bucharest ('Bucharest (1881-1916, 1918-1947); Iasi (1916-1918)').
1918, January: the Bolsheviks take Kyiv from the Rada.
1918, January: Bolshevik forces take the left bank and the Dnieper bend.
1918, January: Bolshevik forces advance on Kiev, taking "Yekaterinoslav (January 9), Aleksandrovsk (January 15), and Poltava (January 20)" after Kharkov (26 December 1917).

1918: the Basmachi rebellion 'started in earnest' after the February assault on Kokand, under Irgash Bey, 'Supreme Leader of the Islamic Army'; its roots lay in the anti-conscription violence of 1916.
1918, 24 February: Estonia declares independence.
16 February 1918: Lithuania is re-established as a state.
1918, February-March: the I Polish Corps holds six Belarusian districts.

18 February 1918: Operation Faustschlag (infobox '18 February - 3 March 1918'): 'the German and Austro-Hungarian forces started a major three-pronged offensive'; 'Ukrainian troops and the Austro-Hungarian Army had secured Odessa'; after Brest-Litovsk 'capturing the whole of Ukraine'.
1918, February: German troops occupy Estonia.
9 February 1918: the Central Powers sign a peace with Ukraine.
18 February 1918: Operation Faustschlag.
1918, 2 February: the siege of the Babruysk fortress begins.
1917 November to 1918 February: Soviet power is set up across Russia proper.
1918: Soviet forces storm Kokand.
1918: Kokand surrenders.
1918: the Kokand Autonomy ends on 22 February.
1918, 9 February: Muravyov's Bolshevik forces take Kyiv.
1918, 9 February: the Bolshevik forces "entered Kiev under Mikhail Muravyov's [command] on February 9"; on the same day the UNR signed the Treaty of Brest-Litovsk with the Central Powers.
1918, 11 March: the Babruysk fortress falls ('the fortress fell on 11 March, but the German army forced the Polish forces to give over the fortress').
1918, 3 March: Brest-Litovsk: Soviet Russia "gave up claims to Finland, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, most of Belarus, and Ukraine" and returned Kars, Ardahan and Batum to the Ottomans.
1918, 3 March: Soviet Russia gives up Ukraine at Brest-Litovsk.
1918, 1 March: the Ukrainian army returns to Kyiv.

1918, 1 March: the combined forces "retook Kiev on March 1", "pushing the Bolsheviks out of Right Bank Ukraine" (the Ukrainian War of Independence page: "Kyiv was taken on 1 March by a force of 450,000 German troops"); the counterpart is the German Empire as the lead of the Central Powers' force, with the UNR.
1918, 22 April: the Seim proclaims Transcaucasia an independent federative republic at Tiflis.
1918: the Turkestan Soviet Federative Republic is proclaimed at Tashkent.
1918: the Turkestan republic replaces the governor-generalship; whether Bukhara's protectorate (and Khiva's, below) passed to it is on no page (the TASSR page 'does not describe their relationship').
1918: as for Bukhara; the khanate falls in February 1920 (khanate-of-khiva dossier).
1918, 30 April: the Turkestan ASSR is formed inside the RSFSR; it is the RSFSR's autonomous republic until it is disbanded on 27 October 1924.
1918: the Turkestan Soviet Federative Republic is proclaimed at Tashkent.
1918, April: the Ottoman army holds Batum and presses on Kars.
1918, 25 April: Kars is evacuated.
1918, 29 April: Skoropadsky's coup turns the republic into the Ukrainian State (Hetmanate).
1918, spring: the rest of the Soviet-held land (Kharkov, Poltava, Yekaterinoslav, Aleksandrovsk) passes to the Central Powers.
9 April 1918 (27 March O.S.): Bessarabia joins Romania.
28 May 1918: the Armenian National Council declares Armenia's independence.
28 May 1918: the Azerbaijani National Council proclaims independence after the Transcaucasian federation falls.
1918, 26 May: Georgia declares independence at Tiflis.
21 May 1918: the Ottoman offensive in Armenia; at Abaran, Karakilisa and Sardarabad 'local Armenian forces emerged victorious'.

1918, spring: after the Treaty of Brest-Litovsk 'German forces then recaptured much of the Ukrainian territory under the control of the Bolsheviks, including Kyiv itself', and the Ukrainian State (established 29 April 1918, 'Client state of the German Empire') governed the Kiev, Chernigov, Kharkov, Poltava, Yekaterinoslav, Volhynia and Podolia governorates.
1918, 21 May: the corps is disbanded.
1918: the Treaty of Bucharest gives Bulgaria Southern Dobruja and the south of Northern Dobruja.
1918, 26 May: the Seim dissolves and the Georgian members proclaim the Democratic Republic of Georgia.
1918, 28 May: Armenia declares independence, 'two days later' than 26 May.
1918, 28 May: Azerbaijan proclaims its independence the same day as Armenia.
1918, 26-28 May: the war passes to the successors.
1918, 26-28 May: the federation ends.
4 June 1918: the Treaty of Batum ends the fighting and leaves Armenia 11,396 km2 (infobox; 13,000 km2 in the text).
1918: the Ottoman IV Corps re-enters Persia.
1918, June: the Czechoslovak Legion "captured Samara" in June (the page gives no day), which enabled "the first anti-Bolshevik local government in Siberia, the Komuch, formed on 8 June".

1918, 13 June: "On 13 June, Whites formed the Provisional Siberian Government in Omsk" after White officers' organizations overthrew the Bolsheviks there (no date); the Legion "quickly occupied" Petropavl, Kurgan, Novonikolaevsk and Mariinsk and "took Tyumen" in July.
1918: Ashgabat rises against the Tashkent Bolsheviks.
1918, July: the constitution gives the state its name, the Russian Socialist Federative Soviet Republic (RSFSR); the page gives no day.
1918, July: White Russian troops under Kappel "took Syzran" (the page gives only the month); the Komuch's People's Army.
1918, July: "Radola Gajda took Irkutsk" with the Czechoslovak forces; the Legion also "quickly occupied" Nizhneudinsk and Kansk after Chelyabinsk.
1918: the Ashkhabad rising takes Transcaspia.
1918: Japanese troops land at Vladivostok and occupy the Maritime Provinces.
August 1918: the column leaves Mozambique.
August 1918: the German column enters Northern Rhodesia.
August 1918: the German column leaves Portuguese Mozambique.
1918, 3 August: Japanese, British, French and American troops "landed at Vladivostok" (the page does not say when Soviet power fell in the Far East).
1918, 23 September: the Ufa Act makes the Provisional All-Russian Government "the sole bearer of the supreme power in the whole space of the Russian state".
1918, September: the Serbian army's liberation of Vardar Macedonia.
September 1918: the Austro-Hungarian forces leave Albania.

September 1918: 'In September 1918, the Entente forces broke through the Central Powers' lines north of Thessaloniki, and within days Austro-Hungarian forces began to withdraw from Albania' (Principality of Albania page; the albania dossier /ledger/5 has the same).
15 September 1918: 'The Ottoman Army of Islam and its Azeri allies, led by Nuri Pasha, entered Baku on 15 September'; the republic's government makes it the capital.
September 1918: the capital moves from Ganja to Baku.
1919: the eastern Macedonian cells return to the Cliopatria shape.
30 September 1918: the Macedonian front ends.
1918: Bulgaria asks for an armistice and gives up the occupied Serbian lands.
1918: the armistice orders Bulgaria out of Greek territory.

1918, 23 September: the Ufa Act makes the Provisional All-Russian Government "the sole bearer of the supreme power in the whole space of the Russian state" (russian-state /ledger/0); the Urals and Orenburg were already outside Soviet control (the Czech revolt page dates only Chelyabinsk, 14 May 1918) and are counted from the founding of the state; the pages opened give no 1918 dates for Yekaterinb
1918, September: the Urals pass to the new state with the Ufa Conference.
1918: the Bulgarian occupation ends.
1918, 14-15 September: the French and Serbian assault at Dobro Pole.
1918, 30 September: the Macedonian front ends at noon ('On 29 September the Bulgarians were granted the Armistice of Salonica'; 'The Macedonian front ended at noon on 30 September 1918').
5 October 1918: Faisal announces an Arab government at Damascus.
1918: Czechoslovakia is proclaimed (infobox 'Proclamation 28 October 1918'); 'Czechoslovakia was founded in October 1918', Masaryk first president from 14 November 1918.
30 October 1918: Imam Yahya's northern Yemen becomes independent of the Ottoman Empire.
29 October 1918: the State of Slovenes, Croats and Serbs is proclaimed at Zagreb.
October 1918: Austria-Hungary 'occupied Montenegro from 15 January 1916 to October 1918' (Kingdom of Montenegro page; the montenegro dossier /ledger/12 has the same).

28-30 October 1918: Czech politicians take over in Prague (28 October), the Czechs and Slovaks proclaim Czechoslovakia (28 October) and the Slovaks do the same on 30 October; Czechoslovakia is the infobox successor.
29 October 1918: the State of Slovenes, Croats and Serbs is proclaimed; the page's sentence names 'the Slavs in both portions of what remained of Austria-Hungary'.

31 October 1918: Hungary repudiates the Compromise of 1867 ('On 17 October 1918, the Hungarian Parliament voted in favour of terminating the union with Austria'); 'Karolyi followed suit on 16 November, proclaiming the Hungarian Democratic Republic'.
30 October 1918: German-Austria acts as a state.

28 October 1918: the Polish Liquidation Committee is 'Created on 28 October 1918' by Polish members of the Austrian parliament, seat Krakow, to keep order in 'the former Austrian part of partitioned Poland'; infobox successors of Austria-Hungary: 'Polish Liquidation Committee', 'Kingdom of Poland'.

1 November 1918: 'The West Ukrainian People's Republic was proclaimed on 1 November 1918' at Lviv, 'Until November 13, 1918, the state was officially known as the Ukrainian State'; it 'controlled most of Eastern Galicia from November 1918 to July 1919'.

28 November 1918 (Bukovina) and 1 December 1918 (Transylvania): 'The union of Bukovina with Romania is declared' and 'the union of Transylvania with the Kingdom of Romania on 1 December 1918'; Trianon confirmed 'Transylvania, part of Banat and other territories'.

25 November 1918: the Great National Assembly at Novi Sad 'declared the accession' of 'Banat, Bačka and Baranja' to the Kingdom of Serbia, seceding from the 'already collapsed Austria-Hungary'; Syrmia joined on 24 November (serbs dossier /ledger/28).

3 November 1918 (occupation) and 10 September 1919 (treaty): Saint-Germain gave Italy 'The southern half of the former Tyrolean crownland up to the Brenner Pass' and 'the Austrian Littoral', 'the Imperial Free City of Trieste' and Istria; the Villa Giusti armistice was signed on 3 November 1918 (Austria-Hungary page).
31 October 1918: Austria-Hungary dissolves.
October 1918: Austria-Hungary dissolves and with it the crown land.
8 October 1918: French troops land at Beirut.
6-7 October 1918: the Germans hand over the administration and the Regency Council declares independence.
19 October 1918: the eastern regions are claimed by the West Ukrainian People's Republic after the dissolution of Austria-Hungary; it 'briefly declared the independence of Eastern Galicia'.
October 1918: the Austro-Hungarian occupation ends ('from 15 January 1916 to October 1918').
October 1918: Syria passes out of Ottoman hands.
1918: the Armistice of Mudros (30 October 1918) ends the Ottoman occupation of northern Persia; the infobox lists the Ottoman withdrawal.
1918, 3 and 8 October: the Directory forces abandon Syzran (3 October) and Samara (8 October) to the Red Army.
1918, 3 October: Syzran abandoned to the Red Army ("October 3, 1918: Syzran was abandoned").
1918, 8 October: Samara, the Komuch capital, abandoned ("October 8, 1918: Samara was abandoned").
1918, 9 October: the government moves from Ufa to Omsk because of the Red Army's approach.
1918, October: the Volga-Ural front opens as Boldyrev organises three fronts (Western, South-Western, Siberian) and the Red Army takes the Volga bank; zone drawn from the cities the page names.
1918: Latvia declares independence at Riga on 18 November 1918 (infobox 'Declared: 18 November 1918') after breaking away from the Russian Empire.
11 November 1918: Poland is reborn.
1918 (16 November): the Tripolitanian Republic is proclaimed.
1918: the German Republic is proclaimed on 9 November 1918 (infobox 'Proclaimed: 9 November 1918'); the National Assembly met at Weimar from 6 February to 11 August 1919.
1 November 1918: the West Ukrainian People's Republic is proclaimed at Lviv.
November 1918: France takes Alsace-Lorraine back.
1918: the Reichsland ends.
November 1918: after the Armistice of Mudros (30 October) the Ottoman army leaves the Erivan Governorate and Armenia grows by about 16,000 km2.
Late November 1918: Andranik's offensive into Karabakh.
1 November 1918: Serbian forces enter Belgrade after the Vardar Offensive of September 1918.
11 November 1918: Italy holds most of Albania.
November 1918: French forces hold Korçë and Shkodër.
3 November 1918: the armistice of Villa Giusti.
November 1918 (page silent): the occupation of Wallachia ends with the Central Powers' collapse.
November 1918 (page silent): the Austro-Hungarian zone in Ukraine ends with the collapse; no date on the page.
November 1918: infobox 'Armistice, withdrawal of German forces: 3 November 1918'; Governor Anton Liposcak 'resigned on 2 November 1918' after Austria-Hungary dissolved.
17 November 1918: Allied (British) troops arrive in Baku after the Armistice of Mudros (30 October) replaced the Turkish troops.
Late 1918: Andranik's Armenians seize Karabakh.
14 November 1918: the British enter Mosul.

14 November 1918: after the Armistice of Mudros (30 October 1918) Cobbe 'continued to advance on Mosul in the face of Turkish protests' and 'British troops marched unopposed into the city on the 14 November 1918'; 'The ownership of Mosul Province and its rich oil fields became an international issue'.
November 1918: the duchy ends in the German Revolution.
8 November 1918: the duke abdicates.
14 November 1918: the grand duke renounces the throne.

November 1918 (the page's infobox date is 9 November; the text gives no abdication day): infobox 'German Revolution: November 9, 1918'; 'when the last grand duke, Frederick Augustus II, abdicated'; 'Oldenburg became a constituent state of the Weimar Republic as the Free State of Oldenburg.'
1918, 19 November: the Germans hand power back to the Estonian government (the page: they had to 'return power to the Estonian government on 19 November 1918').
November 1918: Bremen, a free city with no monarch, passes from the Empire's member states to a state of the Weimar Republic.
November 1918: Hamburg, a free city with no monarch, passes from the Empire's member states to a state of the Weimar Republic.
November 1918: Lübeck, a free city with no monarch, passes from the Empire's member states to a state of the Weimar Republic.
